sentences.text: JUDGMENT Claimants in M.V.C.No.1515 of 2014 on the file of the II Additional Small Causes Judge and XXVIII ACMM, Bengaluru (for short, hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal') have filed this appeal challenging the impugned judgment and award dated 03.08.2015 passed in the said case praying for enhancement of the compensation.

entities.text: II Additional Small Causes Judge and XXVIII ACMM, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Even though this matter is slated for admission, with the consent of both the parties, it is taken up for final disposal.
3. We refer the parties as per their rank before the Tribunal.
They met with an accident due to rash and negligent driving of lorry bearing Registration No.KA-05-D-0204 by its driver.
As a result of which, both the riders fell down and Shivakumar @ Shivakumar Nayak had sustained grievous injuries and he succumbed to the injuries at the spot.
The deceased was aged about 35 years at the time of the accident and was serving as a Fabricator at Pooja Engineering and was earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
Claimants being his wife, parents and son, have contended that they were depending upon earning of the deceased.
With these reasons, prayed to award compensation of Rs.25 Lakhs.
5. The Respondent No.1/Insurer has denied the contentions of the claimants and further contended that accident was taken place due to rash and negligent riding of vehicle by the deceased.
Hence, the claimants are not entitled for compensation from the respondent.
The amount of compensation claimed is exorbitant.

The liability of Respondent No.1 is restricted to terms and conditions of NC:
2023:KHC:33692-DB policy of Insurance Company.
With these reasons, prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
6. From the rival contentions of the parties, the Tribunal had framed necessary issues, for consideration.
7. The claimants have examined PW-1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P10.
The respondents have not lead evidence.

sentences.text: After hearing both the sides and appreciating the pleadings and evidence on record, Tribunal had held that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the lorry by its driver.

The Tribunal had assessed the age of the deceased as 33 years; added 50% of income towards his future prospects; deducted 1/4th of income towards personal expenses, applied multiplier as '16'
and awarded following amount of compensation:
Sl.No.
Particulars

Amount (Rs.) 1 Loss of dependency 15,12,000 2 Loss of estate 20,000 3 Loss of love and affection 12,000 NC: 2023:KHC:33692-DB 4 Loss of consortium 25,000 5 Loss of care and guidance for minor children 25,000 6
Funeral expenses 25,000 TOTAL 16,19,000 9.
Being aggrieved by the said judgment and awarded dated 03.08.2015, claimants have preferred this appeal, for enhancement.
10. We have heard arguments of learned Counsels for both side.
The learned Advocate for the appellants vehemently contended that the claimants had produced wage certificate/pay-slip to prove the income of the deceased as Rs.10,000/- per month.
The Tribunal without any reasons has rejected the same.
The amount of compensation awarded under the other heads are meager and therefore, prayed to enhance the same.
11. The learned Advocate for the Insurer/ Respondent has submitted that claimant had not proved pay-slip by examining author of said document.
Therefore, the Tribunal had rightly rejected the said document and assessed notional income as Rs.7,000/- per NC: 2023:KHC:33692-DB month.
The Tribunal has wrongly added 50% of income towards future prospects in place of 40%, since the deceased was not having any permanent employment.

The amount of compensation awarded under the other heads are not in accordance with law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS1 and therefore,
prayed to dismiss the appeal.

entities.text: NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
12. The following question arises for our determination:
"Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?"
13.

The Tribunal after appreciating the pleadings and evidence on record has held that the accident had taken place due to rash and negligent driving of lorry by its driver and due to the accident,
Shivakumar @ Shivakumar Nayak sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
The said finding is on the basis (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2023:KHC:33692-DB of the materials available on record and it does not call for any interference.
The said findings is also not challenged by the respondents.

14. Though claimants have contended that deceased was earning Rs.10,000/- per month as salary by serving as a Fabricator in Pooja Engineering, but they have not examined the author of the certificate, i.e., Ex.P8.
Even they have not produced corroborative documents to prove the said fact.
Mere production of some certificate cannot be accepted as the gospel truth.

Therefore, the Tribunal Vanajakshi vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Com Ltd on 15 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171997078/
4 has rightly not accepted Ex.P8.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The appellant who had not proved the said document cannot contend that the Tribunal has committed an error in not accepting the said document.
Since claimants have failed to prove detail income of deceased, his notional income is to be assessed.

While settlement of motor vehicle compensation cases before the Lok-Adalath, for an accident taken place during the year 2014, income of the victim of an accident is considered as Rs.8,500/- per NC:
2023:KHC:33692-DB month, same could be applied to the facts of the present case.

15. In the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra), when a victim of an accident is not having any permanent employment, 40% of his income is to be added towards future prospects if his age is below 40 years.
In this case, the Tribunal, on the basis of materials available held that age of the deceased was 33 years.
Therefore, 40% of income has to be added towards future prospects.
The deceased left behind him four defendants and hence, 1/4th of his income towards personal expenses.
Undisputedly the multiples applicable in this case is '16'.

Hence, claimants are entitled compensation under the head 'loss of dependency' is as under:
 Income per Rs.8,500  month  Add 40% Rs.3,400  towards future  prospects
Total Rs.11,900  Less 1/4th  towards  personal  - 10 -  NC: 2023:KHC:33692-DB  expenses Rs.2,975
Net income per Rs.8,925  month
The appellants are entitled for compensation of {(8925X12X16(multiplier)}=Rs.17,13,600/- under the head 'loss of dependency'.

16. As per the law laid down in the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra) and also the recent and unreported judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of SHRI RAM GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. BHAGAT SINGH RAWAT & ORS2, the claimants are entitled for fixed sum of compensation under the conventional head and every three years from the date of rendering of the judgment in the case of PRANAY SETHI (referred supra), 10% is to be enhanced.

18.
The learned Advocate for the Insurer has vehemently contended that at the time of passing the orders on I.A.No.1 of 2022 and 2 of 2022, delay was condoned by denying the interest.

Therefore,
claimants are not entitled for interest for the period of 1607 days in filing the applications to condone delay in recalling of dismissal order of this appeal.
19. The said submission is not acceptable.
While disposing of I.A.No.1 of 2022 and 2 of 2022 by order dated 01.07.2022, this Court has not ordered that delay was condoned by denying the interest for the delayed period.
On the contrary, imposed cost of Rs.1,000/-.
Therefore, claimants are entitled for interest on the enhanced amount from the date of petition till its payment.

20. For the aforesaid discussion, we answer the above said question partly in affirmative and pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is partly allowed.
